newsitem.title: UK: Britain sends reconnaissance troops to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Britain sends reconnaissance troops to Zaire.

text.p: Britain sent a 43-strong military reconnaissance party to central Africa on Friday to see if it can help ease the humanitarian crisis in Zaire.
Its job is to check the conditions on the ground for any contribution that Britain might make to a multinational force.
Prime Minister John Major pledged that the rules of engagement for British troops would soon be clarified.
"British troops intrinsically have the right to defend themselves and would certainly do so. No one is going to take any risks with the lives of British troops," he told reporters.
Major, who was in telephone contact with U.S. President Bill Clinton during the night, said he hoped more troops could follow the reconnaissance team as speedily as possible.
"There isn't a great deal of time and speed in many ways is of the essence. So we will not delay, the faster it can be done, the better," he said.
The reconnaissance party, headed by rapid deployment force chief Brigadier John Thompson, flew initially to Nairobi and Entebbe to assess the use of their airports as staging posts to Zaire.
The party will then travel to Goma and Bukavu in Zaire for an on-the-spot review of the situation. It will return to Britain on Monday to brief military chiefs.
Britain has cautioned it would not send a larger force until the nature of its mission to help more than a million starving refugees was absolutely clear.
Major says Western governments have a strong moral obligation to help ease the crisis and Britain is ready in principle to join a Canadian-led international force.
But he told parliament on Thursday that the situation on the ground was complex, the terrain was very tough and there was no clear ceasefire between Tutsi rebels and their Hutu foes.
